text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - UK blue chips ended a lethargic session slightly higher as institutional investors continued to keep their distance from a market currently plagued by a host of uncertainties. "It's been another nothing day. The funds are just sitting on their cash," the head of trading at a large brokerage said. The FTSE 100 index ended 4.3 points higher at 4,298.9.

FRANKFURT - German equities advanced strongly over the course of bourse trade to end just off the session highs after the widely-expected decision by the Bundesbank to keep key rates unchanged, shares edged up earlier on after the Ifo institute's March business index turned out worse than expected, boosting the debt market. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,383.25 up 29.80 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,361.80.

PARIS - French shares closed slightly lower due to a lower domestic bond market and despite gains on Wall Street, bond prices fell due to resurgent doubts over whether France can hit its deficit reduction targets. The CAC-40 index closed 5.79 points or 0.22 percent lower at 2,615.18.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended firmer in selective trading, with the focus on pharmaceuticals Novartis and Roche and on cement prducer Holderbank. The All-share SPI gained 24.93 to close at 2,952.25.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed slightly higher, helped by a rebound in the financial sector and fresh buying in a wide range of issues, but a retreat in major blue-chip issues capped the upside. The 225-share Nikkei average rose 62.21 points or 0.35 percent to close at 18,093.41.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks gave up small early gains to close moderately down, chiefly due to weakness in the outlook for property developers and a reassessment of the interest rate outlook. The Hang Seng Index closed 65.08 points lower at 12,516.23, well off the day's high of 12,635.52.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market finished modestly firmer as investors mostly ignored a strong gain on Wall Street on Wednesday and focused buying attention on a handful of blue chip issues. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 6.8 points firmer at 2,413.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares ended weaker following another bad day on the bullion markets and a poor set of results from Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd. The international price of the yellow metal hovered precariously near to the $340 an ounce level, spreading yet more doom and gloom in an index that has become well-used to bad news. The Gold index finished 2.1 points down at 1,250.6, Industrials index ended up 10.4 points at 8,238.7 and the All-shares index drifted off 0.8 points to close at 6,976.
